spans.value: Auto-hide the Island.
Turn on
Auto-hide the Island

in Settings → General, from the View menu, or with ⌘⌥B on macOS (Ctrl+Alt+B on Windows and Linux), and the page fills the whole window. Point at the top edge of the window, rest the pointer near the top, or press ⌘L (Ctrl+L) to bring the Island back; it slides away again once you move off it. It's off by default.
Tab Archive.
Turn on
Archive inactive tabs

in Settings → General, and loose tabs you haven't looked at for 12 hours, a day, 7 days or 30 days close themselves into an Archive. Pinned, grouped and private tabs are never archived, and neither is a tab that is playing media or holding something you typed. Find archived tabs in the ⌘L panel, or in History →
Archived tabs
(or
/archive
), and restore them with one click. The Archive stays on this device and keeps each tab for 30 days. It's off by default; a new profile offers it during setup.
Sunrise Gold.
A new macOS app icon: the Sunrise in glass over gold, soft in Light and polished in Dark. Choose it in Settings → General → App icon.
What's New.
After an update that adds features, Blanc opens a page on blanc.day showing the highlights, once.
Settings → General is grouped into cards:
Island, Appearance, Start Page, Search and Browsing. The theme setting is now labeled
Theme
A panel opened by hover closes when you move away
from it, unless you used it.
On macOS, the window buttons sit where Safari and Finder put them.
Your own Start Page image.
Open
Customize
on the Start Page and choose
Your image
under Wallpaper to show a JPEG or PNG of your own, up to 25 MB.
Wash
(Auto, Light, Dark or Spotlight) and
Fade

keep the page readable over it. Blanc keeps a resized copy on this device only, with location, camera and time details removed. It isn't synced, and private tabs never show it. Settings → General → Start Page image offers the same choice.
A Start Page color.
Choose
Color
under Wallpaper to paint the Start Page in one of the eight colors Spaces use, as a
Soft
Solid
or
Gradient
fill. Turn on
Match each space's color

, and a window that belongs to a space shows that space's color instead. The color settings sync with Profile Sync; an image chosen on this device still takes priority here. Private tabs never show the color.
Tab group colors.

A group can take one of eight colors, the same ones Spaces use, or none, which is the default. A colored group's block in the ⌘L panel and on the vertical tabs rail takes a light tint, its name gets a dot, and its tabs' dots in the Island take the color.
A menu for each group.
Right-click a group's header, or press the ⋮ that appears when you point at it. The menu holds the group's name, its color,
New Tab in Group
Move Group to New Window
Ungroup
and
Close Group
Put ungrouped tabs anywhere.

Drag an ungrouped tab above, between or below your groups in the ⌘L panel or on the vertical tabs rail, or move it with ⌥⇧↑ and ⌥⇧↓. Each run of ungrouped tabs gets its own place in the Island's dots and in ⌘1–9. New tabs still land at the bottom, and windows and spaces saved before this update open exactly as before.
More in the tab menu.
Right-click a tab for
New Tab Below
Close Tabs Above
and
Close Tabs Below
, which leave pinned tabs alone and can be reopened in one go, and
Mute Site
, which mutes every tab on that site, including ones you open there later, until you quit Blanc.
Pinned pages.

A pinned tab remembers the page you pinned it on. When you reopen Blanc after quitting normally, each pinned tab starts back on its pinned page. After a crash, it reopens on the page you were on. Right-click a pinned tab for
Back to Pinned Page
or
Replace Pinned Page with Current
Open the Island on hover.
Turn on
Open the Island on hover
in Settings → General, and resting the pointer on the Island's address for a moment opens the panel. It's off by default.
Site icons on bang rows.

Bangs in the ⌘L panel now show each site's icon. Blanc uses an icon you already have from your own visits when it can. Otherwise it asks blanc.day's icon server for that one site's icon and keeps a small copy on this device. Private tabs never ask.
Tooltips throughout the Island.
Buttons in the ⌘L panel and on the resting Island now show their tooltip reliably when you point at them.
Links open as ungrouped tabs.
A link opened in a new tab from a grouped tab now opens ungrouped, at the bottom, like any new tab, instead of joining the group.
Quieter private mode.
Private tabs no longer draw dashed outlines. The Island's private marker is a small
Private
label that shows its × when you point at it, the header on a private Start Page matches its wallpaper, and the private Start Page shows the date.
The Start Page footer sits on the wallpaper
instead of on a solid band, shaded to match each wallpaper and time of day so it stays easy to read.
The Island's reload, favorite and close buttons match
in size and hover, and a button you can't use right now is dimmed instead of nearly disappearing.
A clearer Glance icon
in the ⌘L panel, and larger pin, mute, Glance and close buttons on tab rows.
On Linux, Invite a Friend
now copies the invite when no mail app opens it, and says so.
The scroll bar in the ⌘L panel
and on the vertical tabs rail no longer covers the end of each row.
Dragging a tab to the top of your unpinned tabs
now works when you have no pinned tabs.
Bangs.
In the ⌘L or Ctrl+L panel, type an exclamation mark and a site's code before your search, like
!yt lofi
, and Blanc opens that site's results directly, whichever search engine you use. The code also works at the end (
lofi !yt
), and a code on its own, like
!yt
, opens the site. Type

on its own to see the bangs you used recently and a set of popular ones, then keep typing to search more than 10,000 bangs by code or site name. The list is Kagi's open bang list. It ships inside Blanc and changes only with a Blanc update, so Blanc never looks bangs up online. Add your own bangs, or turn bangs off, in Settings → General. Blanc doesn't ask your search engine for suggestions while a bang is in the box. The bangs you used recently stay on this device, and private tabs don't record them.
Add a device to Sync with a code.
On a device that already syncs, go to Settings → Sync and choose
Add another device
. It shows a code that works for ten minutes. On the new device, choose
Add this device to my sync
and enter the code. Your sync name and passphrase still work too. A device that started its own sync by mistake can join yours with
Connect to a different sync with a code
Copy recovery code
puts a code on the clipboard for your password manager, which also adds a device.
Name your devices.
Right-click a device under
Other devices
in the ⌘L panel and choose
Rename Device…
, or set
This device's name
in Settings → Sync. The name shows on your other devices running 1.36.0; earlier versions keep showing the computer's name.
Invite a Friend.
Help → Invite a Friend…
, or
/invite

in the ⌘L or Ctrl+L panel, opens a new email in your mail app with a short invite and a link to download Blanc. You choose who it goes to and send it yourself. Blanc sends nothing and doesn't learn who you invited. If no mail app opens, the invite is copied so you can paste it.
Rename, ungroup or close a group from its header.
Right-click a group's header in the ⌘L panel or on the vertical tabs rail and choose
Rename Group…
Ungroup
or
Close Group
About Blanc shows the Chromium version
Blanc runs on.
What's new after an update.
Once Blanc restarts into a new version, the Start Page footer shows a
What's new in 1.36.0

pill that opens that release's notes on blanc.day. It stays for seven days, or until you open it or close it with its ×. While it shows, it takes the place of the Patron pill. Fresh installs and private tabs don't show it.
A tidier ⌘L panel.
Recently closed

is a band under Pinned. It's folded each time the panel opens; unfold it to see every closed tab Blanc keeps (up to 25), newest first. Drag its header to move it among your groups. Each window remembers where you put it, and so does each space.
The footer is one line:
New tab
Private
Other devices
and the tools. Tabs from your other devices moved from the bottom of the list into an
Other devices
drawer above the footer, shown only when another device shares its tabs.
A tab in Glance shows a Glance icon beside pin and close instead of a "glance" label.
Labels in the panel use sentence case, and slash commands and bang codes sit in small chips.
Group names keep the capitals you type.
Matching still ignores case, so
/group research
joins a group named Research. Group names saved before this update get a capital first letter once.
Finish setup leads with Make Blanc your default
on macOS and Windows, and checks it off once Blanc is your default browser. If you finish setup on a new install without switching, Blanc asks once more, between 12 hours and 14 days later, with
Set as default
and
Not now
, and never again.
A Mac now appears on your other devices under its computer name, not a name taken from the network such as "mac.lan".
On Windows, Blanc and its installer name Bananify Creative as the company, so Windows Firewall's prompt and Settings → Apps show Bananify Creative instead of GitHub, Inc.
Open tabs could stop syncing
to your other devices while one tab's title kept changing, such as a timer or an unread count.
Name your tabs.
Right-click a tab and choose
Rename Tab…
, or type
/rename
and a name in the ⌘L or Ctrl+L panel, to give a tab a name of your own instead of the page's title.
Reset Tab Title
in the same menu, or
/rename

on its own, goes back to the page title. The name stays when you browse to another site, when the tab goes quiet, when you move it to a new window, reopen it after closing it, save it in a space or restart Blanc. With Profile Sync sharing your open tabs, your other devices show the name too. History and Favorites keep the page's own title, and a private tab's name is forgotten when Blanc quits.
Open a link straight into Glance.
Right-click a link and choose
Open Link in Glance
to see it beside the page you're on. Typing
/glance
in the ⌘L or Ctrl+L panel opens the Glance picker, and
/glance
followed by a few words opens it showing only the matching tabs.
Back and Reload in Glance.
The page you keep beside your main page in Glance now has its own Back button and Reload (or Stop) button.
Back and Forward shortcuts:
⌘[ and ⌘] on macOS, Alt+Left and Alt+Right on Windows and Linux.
Glance follows the page you're using.

When you click into the page in Glance, Reload, Close Tab, Find, zoom, Print, Back, Forward, mouse gestures and the 1Password fill act on that page instead of the main page. When that page opens a link in a new tab, the link opens in Glance; links you open in the background still open as background tabs. ⌘L, ⌘T, ⌘1–9, the shield and slash commands still act on the main page.

Glance opens and closes with a short slide and fade (a plain fade when Reduce Motion is on), its picker rows look like the ⌘L list, and a private tab in Glance shows the private label. While Glance is open the Island hides its tab dots to keep room for the address.
Blanc's interface text is now set in Instrument Sans. In light mode, the Start Page and the Favorites, History, Downloads and Settings sheets use a new warm off-white palette, Blanc White.
The Sunrise app icon and the Sunrise mark inside Blanc are redrawn from a vector drawing, so they are sharper at large sizes on macOS, Windows and Linux.
Blanc no longer starts its screen-sharing helper every time it launches. It starts the first time a site asks to share your screen, so idle Blanc uses a little less memory.
Updated to Electron 44.8.0 and Chromium 152.0.7977.167 for upstream fixes. The optional uBlock Origin blocker remains available on this version.
PDFs show in Blanc's built-in viewer again.
Since v1.20.0 every PDF opened as an empty viewer: a dark toolbar with no pages.
Importing Favorites from Chrome could find nothing when you were signed in to Chrome.

Recent Chrome keeps a signed-in profile's bookmarks in a separate file, which Blanc didn't read. Blanc now imports from both files, without duplicates. This also applies to Edge, Brave, Chromium and Vivaldi.
With uBlock Origin chosen, some requests could get through unblocked while uBlock Origin reloaded its filter lists
, which it does shortly after launch, after a list update and after you change filters. Pages now wait for the reload to finish, usually less than a second.
Shortened slash commands put the command into the name:
/gr work
made a group named "/gr work",
/sav
and
/spa
did the same, and
/the dark
did nothing. They now work like the full commands.

In Glance, sound from a video in the Glance page now plays, and a site in the Glance page can ask to share your screen. Moving the main page to a new window, or closing the group that holds it, now makes the Glance page the main page, and closing the Glance page returns the keyboard to the main page.

Glance's layout: the divider stays under the pointer while you drag it. When Glance is stacked, the Island is centered on the window and the picker fits. On Windows and Linux the window buttons stay readable over the Glance header, and with Glance open the Island no longer slides under the macOS window buttons, or under the Windows and Linux ones with vertical tabs.
⌘⇧G (Ctrl+Shift+G on Windows and Linux) opens the Glance picker even with one tab open, where it explains that Glance needs another tab. Closing Glance while its picker is open closes the picker too.
Screen readers now announce when you reorder tabs in the ⌘L list.
Kagi, or your own search engine.
Settings → General → Search engine now offers Kagi, and
Custom…
for any search engine that puts your search words in its address, such as SearXNG. Paste that address with
%s
where the words go, for example
https://searx.example.org/search?q=%s
. It syncs with your other settings when Profile Sync is on. Plain
http://
addresses work only for this computer or your home network.

Kagi shows live suggestions as you type, like the other search engines. Kagi needs a Kagi account, and private tabs don't share your sign-in, so a Kagi search in a private tab asks you to sign in. A custom search engine shows no suggestions, so nothing you type is sent before you press Enter.
In Settings, the lists of sites that skip ad blocking or Dark websites now sit directly under their switches, in one bordered box, and every site has an always-visible × to remove it.

On Linux, a page could stop redrawing and barely respond to scrolling after you came back to its tab: by switching tabs, viewing it beside another tab with Glance, reopening a closed tab, returning to a space or moving it to a new window. These pages now keep drawing.

On Linux, with Settings → General → Quiet inactive tabs turned on, a background tab that keeps data for the current session could come back frozen after it was quieted: it didn't redraw or scroll. It now reloads, redraws and responds to scrolling again when you go back to it.
On Windows and Linux, closing the last window with Blanc's own close button (✕) lost your tabs: the next launch opened only a new tab. Blanc now keeps them, as Quit already did.

On Windows and Linux, closing Blanc's original window while another Blanc window stayed open didn't fully close it: its pages kept running, and it came back with its tabs the next time you started Blanc. It now closes for good. Blanc also no longer opens an extra empty window after restoring only a second window.
Paste and Go with a search operator such as
site:example.com
opened a broken address. It now searches.

In Settings → Privacy & Security, an invalid custom Encrypted DNS address could switch you to a custom address you had saved earlier. It now keeps the provider you had. The error under the field now shows in red, and screen readers announce it.

Blanc's interface is available in Italian, machine-translated, alongside German, Spanish, French and Portuguese (Brazil). If your system uses Italian, Blanc now follows it; choose English or another language any time in Settings → General → Language.
Blanc Spaces, redesigned.

Each space now has a colour and a symbol, shown at the start of the Island; click it to switch, edit, reorder or delete (with Undo). Pick any colour — Blanc keeps the symbol readable in light and dark mode.

Blanc Spaces is free for everyone. Anyone can save, switch between and import spaces, including bringing Spaces over from Arc. Blanc Patron is now simply a way to support Blanc — thank you to every Patron whose support made Spaces possible.

Switching between spaces no longer stops with "Your retained spaces are full." Every switch now goes through. To keep memory in check, Blanc may free up memory used by tabs in spaces you left a while ago; those tabs reload when you go back to them.

On Linux, with Settings → General → Quiet inactive tabs turned on, a background tab that keeps data for the current session could stay loaded instead of freeing up its memory. It now frees it, and reloads when you go back to it.
In Spanish, French and Portuguese, the
/theme
hint and its entry in the slash command reference showed translated appearance names (for example "oscuro" or "sombre"), and typing them after
/theme
did nothing. They now show
system
light
and
dark
, the words
/theme
accepts in every language.
Bring your Spaces over from Arc. In
Bring Your Tabs
(type
/bring-tabs

in the ⌘L or Ctrl+L panel), the new Arc option reads Arc's sidebar and brings each Space you pick, with its pinned tabs, its Today tabs and its folders, which become tab groups. With Blanc Patron, each Arc Space becomes a space in Blanc Spaces; without it, each Space opens in its own window. Tabs load only when you open them. You can also add Arc's top-row Favorites to a Favorites folder named
Arc
. Sign-ins, passwords, history, archived tabs, Notes and Easels stay in Arc, and Blanc only reads Arc's sidebar file without changing it. Arc never came to Linux: there, copy
StorableSidebar.json
from your Mac or PC and choose it with
Choose file…

Blanc's interface is available in German, Spanish, French and Portuguese (Brazil), machine-translated. If your system uses one of these languages, Blanc now follows it (any Portuguese system gets Brazilian Portuguese); choose English or another language any time in Settings → General → Language.
Named Workspaces is now called
Blanc Spaces
, and each saved set of tabs is a space. Type
/space
in the ⌘L or Ctrl+L panel to switch to a space or save the current window as one;
/workspace
still works. Creating spaces is still part of Blanc Patron.
When 1Password login fill isn't set up yet, the prompt's
Open Settings
button now opens Settings at the 1Password card instead of at the top.
Blanc's website is now
blanc.day
. Settings → Help, the About window, the welcome screen's privacy link and the update error messages point there. Older blancbrowser.com links still work.
On Windows and Linux, the keyboard shortcuts sheet showed "Search && Commands". It now reads "Search & Commands".

Opening Blanc while it's already running, for example by opening a link from another app, now just passes the link to the open Blanc. The second launch used to keep starting up in the background on the same profile and then fail.
The start page footer is reorganized. The "ready to move in?" checklist is now a
Finish setup
pill on the left of the footer that opens the list; its × hides the checklist for good, as before.
Customize
sits alone in the middle.
The Blanc Patron reminder is now one
Upgrade to Blanc Patron
pill in the start page footer. Its × hides it on this device for 90 days. Patrons and private tabs still never see it.
Billboard's clock, recent sites and groups are centered vertically in the window, and the clock no longer shows AM/PM.
Start page, onboarding and Settings headings use a narrower cut of Blanc's serif typeface, the same one as blancbrowser.com, and the Billboard clock is set in a lighter weight.

Private tabs are marked more consistently: the "private" chip in the Island, the tag in the expanded tab list and the marker in vertical tabs share one dashed style, and the tag lines up on every row.

Blanc 1.31.0 and later report two facts on their first day, if usage measurement is on: whether Blanc is your default browser, and whether you opened three web pages in regular tabs. Nothing about the pages is sent. The privacy page and FAQ explain the details.
Opening the Island by clicking it no longer makes it blink, and a slow frame now pauses the expand instead of making it jump ahead.
The Tabs step of Bring Your Tabs shows every tab in each window. A window used to show only two or three, with no way to scroll to the rest.

The Island, Blanc's floating address and tab bar, grows slightly as your pointer approaches it. That movement is now smooth at any display refresh rate. It used to update about 60 times a second, which looked stop-start on 120 Hz and faster screens.

Activating a Blanc Patron license key while Polar, the payment service, is busy or down now says Polar is not responding and to try again in a few minutes, instead of saying the key could not be activated.

When Blanc checks an active Patron license and Polar reports that the key is missing, revoked, or expired, Patron now ends. Before, that answer was treated like an outage. A Polar outage still keeps Patron active for up to 30 days, as before.

You can drag to reorder tabs and groups, in the expanded Island and in vertical tabs. Drag a tab within its group, into another group, or out of its group. Dropping a tab on a group's header adds it to that group, even when the group is folded. Drag a group's header to move the whole group, and Cmd/Ctrl+1–9 follow the new order. Pinned tabs stay pinned, and releasing a drag over the page does nothing.
The same moves work from the keyboard: focus a tab or a group header and press Alt+Shift+Up or Alt+Shift+Down (Option+Shift on macOS). Folded groups are skipped.
Settings has a new
About & Trust

section. It shows facts about the installed build, checked on your device: the version, the Electron and Chromium versions, the blocker's filter sources and, on macOS and Windows, the app's code signature. It links to the release, the verification guide, the software bill of materials and the build provenance, and can export diagnostics. Opening it makes no network request.
Intel Macs get every release again. Each release now ships both an Apple Silicon and an Intel build.
Blanc saves its settings, Favorites, history and workspaces in the background instead of pausing the app while it writes to disk. Quitting still saves everything before Blanc closes.
In a Flatpak, Check for Updates says that Flatpak keeps Blanc current instead of showing an unsupported-channel warning.

With uBlock Origin selected, uBO now restarts on its own if it fails while you browse. Pages wait while it restarts instead of loading unfiltered, and the shield shows that it is restarting. After three restarts in 10 minutes, Blanc offers to restart it for you instead.
With uBlock Origin selected, a moment when Blanc itself was busy no longer counts against uBO's time to decide on a request, so pages stop failing after a brief freeze.
On macOS, changing a setting no longer briefly freezes Blanc while it reloads the Dock icon.
On Linux under Wayland, Settings and other sheets appear every time you open them, not only the first time, and the page underneath keeps responding.
On Linux under Wayland, each permission prompt shows its own question instead of the previous one.

Dark websites: while Blanc is dark, it can darken websites that have no dark mode of their own, from the first paint. Turn it on in Settings → General. It is off by default and stays on this device. The Island shield's new
Dark website
switch, or
/dark-site
, darkens or restores a single site. It uses the open-source Dark Reader engine, bundled with Blanc. Embedded frames keep their original colors.
Match site colors, in Settings → General, controls whether the Island bar takes on the color of the page you're on. It is on by default; turn it off to keep the bar on your theme's background.
Interrupted downloads can be resumed, or retried from the original link when resuming isn't possible. Retry reuses the save location you already chose.
On local and private-network addresses, such as a home server with a self-signed certificate, the certificate warning offers
Advanced
and a way to continue. The choice lasts until Blanc quits, applies only to that site and certificate, and is never saved or synced. Public sites keep the warning with no way through.
The start page has one shared frame for all four layouts: the date and moving-in checklist at the top, centered content, and a
Customize
popover in the footer for the layout and dynamic wallpaper.

Ledger is a centered spread, with Favorites beside your tab groups and other devices. Billboard labels its tiles with short site names on one row. Shelf arranges its tiles and cards on one grid sized to how many you have. Tally balances its columns and gives its chart a warmer tint.

With uBlock Origin selected, a slow first install no longer leaves a new start page loading until it finishes, and a slow first start on a fresh profile has 45 seconds, not 15, before it is treated as stalled.

With uBlock Origin selected, the first page you open right after it starts no longer fails to load on a slower computer. For its first 15 seconds, uBO gets 10 seconds instead of 2 to decide on each request; nothing is let through unfiltered while it decides.
A Settings, History or other sheet whose page never finishes loading is removed after 8 seconds instead of leaving an invisible layer over the page.
The new tab and private buttons at the bottom of the Island panel no longer overflow on Windows and Linux in small windows or at 125% zoom.
Optional full uBlock Origin 1.75.0 on Apple Silicon and native Intel Macs, Windows x64, and Linux x64. Click the Island shield, choose your blocker, then use
Restart Blanc
to apply the change.

Blanc styling for uBO’s popup and Dashboard, with filter subscriptions, custom filters, dynamic rules, picker/zapper, logger, and backup/restore. Filter lists can update automatically; executable resources stay pinned to reviewed Blanc releases.

Separate uBO configuration for each regular profile. Blanc Blocker remains the default and protects private tabs; the two blockers keep separate site exceptions. Provider selection and uBO configuration stay outside Profile Sync. General extension-store support is not included.

Automatic return to Blanc Blocker with an explanation if saved uBO selection is unavailable in the running build, preserving uBO configuration. Intel builds running under Rosetta use Blanc Blocker. An available uBO instance that crashes or exceeds its request deadline keeps traffic blocked until recovery or an explicit user choice.
Provider restart and shutdown no longer lose an overlay callback when Electron removes a native child view.
Linux AppImage provider restarts use the upstream extraction launcher and retain Chromium sandbox enforcement. Normal close/relaunch preserves the selected blocker and saved uBO filters.
The Linux sandbox refusal dialog offers
Open Setup Guide
and
Quit
. X11 retains
Copy Link
; Wayland omits clipboard controls. A relaunch with the guide URL omits Open Setup Guide to prevent a loop. Sandbox requirements and system security settings are unchanged.
Supported versions, tested platforms, and integration limits

Settings → Help now shows the running Blanc, Electron and Chromium versions, platform and architecture. Links explain how Blanc works, privacy choices, source code and release notes. Check for updates uses the existing update flow; applying an update still requires restarting.
The background behind the Island follows wallpaper fades and page color changes after loading. Sampling stays on the device; private tabs retain their theme background.

Setup and privacy settings explain search suggestions and pseudonymous usage measurement, their recipients, and when sending starts. Fresh defaults and saved choices are retained. Opening the privacy explanation preserves unsaved setup choices.
Ctrl/Cmd-click and middle-click open eligible website links in new tabs while preserving their navigation and sandbox restrictions.
A rejected Windows update can be retried through Check for Updates without leaving the restart action stuck.
Windows requires a completed publisher check and matching verified installer bytes before installation. If verification cannot complete, installation is deferred for a later retry.

Linux refuses launches that disable Chromium's sandbox, including an AppImage launcher's automatic fallback. On systems that cannot provide the required sandbox, Blanc shows guidance instead of opening browsing windows. This does not change the system's user-namespace or AppArmor configuration.
Authenticate
SHA256SUMS
with its Sigstore bundle using the certificate identity
anthony@bnfy.me
and OIDC issuer
https://github.com/login/oauth
. The same values are published on
Blanc's security page
The folder picker opened by
move ▸
in Favorites now stays above neighboring rows, opens upward when needed, and stays inside the window. With many folders, its options scroll inside the menu while the
new folder…
field remains visible. Opening the picker no longer scrolls the selected favorite out of view.
Escape closes the folder picker and returns focus to its move button; a second Escape closes Favorites.
Favorites group headings now use plain labels and count badges, without the curved bottom divider.
Authenticate
SHA256SUMS
with its Sigstore bundle using the certificate identity
anthony@bnfy.me
and OIDC issuer
https://github.com/login/oauth
. The same values are published on
Blanc's security page
A free, optional time-of-day wallpaper for the start page. Sunrise now follows your local clock through dawn, day, dusk, and night, with no location permission or network requests. Enable
dynamic wallpaper
beside the layout picker or
Time-of-day wallpaper
in Settings.

The wallpaper works in every start-page layout and private tabs. Turning it on or off fades over two seconds; reduced-motion settings switch immediately. If you use Sync, your wallpaper preference follows your devices.

Linux AppImages no longer require FUSE 2. The packaged desktop shortcut also passes URLs correctly and no longer adds unintended command-line arguments. Existing shortcuts may need to be integrated again to receive that correction.
Updated the official Electron runtime to 44.5.1, including upstream security fixes.
Updated dependency inputs to address brace-expansion advisories and the website's devalue advisories.

with its Sigstore bundle using the certificate identity
anthony@bnfy.me
and OIDC issuer
https://github.com/login/oauth
. The same values are published on
Blanc's security page

Settings, Favorites, History, Downloads, Shortcuts, and Bring Your Tabs now share a clearer Sunrise sheet design. Roomier cards, easier-to-scan headings, and controls that fit the minimum window size make everyday tasks less cramped.
History groups visits by day, shows site icons, and lines up visit times. Favorites shows saved site icons or a domain-initial tile when no icon is available.
Downloads lines up status and actions across rows, identifies the source site, and keeps the extension visible on long filenames.
Privacy & Security settings are grouped by topic. Longer explanations can be expanded with
More
without losing any of their detail.
The moving-in checklist and welcome tour are easier to use in a small window or at increased zoom.
A site permission request no longer takes keyboard focus away from the page or an open Island panel.
The Settings section marker now follows scrolling, and Shortcuts shows readable key labels instead of raw accelerator names.

Blanc now gives back the memory of tabs you have not opened in a while. A tab left alone past the delay you choose hands its page back to the system; it keeps its place in the Island, the rail, and the switcher, and reloads when you come back to it. Choose the delay — off, 30 minutes, 1 hour, or 6 hours — under Settings → General → Quiet inactive tabs. It is set to an hour to begin with, and the choice stays on this device.
A quiet tab says so where you pick tabs: its row dims in the ⌘L panel and the vertical rail, and carries the word
quiet
. Screen readers hear the same word. The dim alone would not do — after a relaunch every restored tab is quiet, and a uniformly dim list reads as styling rather than as a state.

Blanc leaves a tab alone when quieting it would cost you something: anything playing or that has played sound, anything muted or pinned, a page with something typed into it or a checkbox you ticked, a page that asks before you leave, a result of a form you submitted, a tab waiting on a permission prompt, a window it opened or was opened by, and a page you have scrolled deep into. The new
/sleep
command quiets every eligible background tab straight away — it skips the waiting and nothing else, and it works even with the delay set to off.
Reopening Blanc is quicker. Restored tabs come back quiet with their titles and site icons already in place, and only the tab you were last using loads.

You can now see when a site is using your microphone or camera. While any tab or pop-out window is recording, a red microphone or camera mark appears in the Island; clicking it lists every site currently listening or watching, and each one has a stop button. Blanc knows a site started recording because it granted the permission itself, so the mark cannot be suppressed by the page — and if a site's own recording ends in a way Blanc cannot observe, the mark stays up rather than going quietly dark. A tab that is recording is never quieted.

Turning the quiet delay off stops Blanc quieting anything new. Tabs that are already quiet stay as they are and come back normally when you open them — switching the setting off never throws away what a quiet tab needs to return.
Permission requests now appear along the bottom of the page instead of beside the Island, where they crowded it, and a request for your microphone or camera shows which one it is asking for.

The island now senses your cursor. Move toward it and it leans your way, rises slightly, and grows — reaching full strength as you arrive and easing back as you leave. You can bring your favorites over from another browser. Blanc reads bookmarks from an installed Chrome, Edge, Brave, Chromium, or Vivaldi profile, keeps their folders, and skips anything already saved, so importing twice doesn't create duplicates. Blanc only goes looking when you press "Look for other browsers", and it only ever opens that browser's bookmarks file — passwords, history, cookies, and open tabs are never read. Firefox and Safari aren't read directly; use the existing "Import HTML…" route for those.

Blanc 1.0.6 fixes the expanded-island click bug that 1.0.4 and 1.0.5 both tried and failed to resolve, and corrects the record on what was actually wrong.

Fixed pinned tabs occasionally becoming unclickable when the expanded island overlapped a site's draggable interface regions. Some sites — typically those built from shared desktop-app UI — mark parts of their own interface as draggable. In a desktop shell those marks become operating-system-level regions that are resolved before the application's own windows are consulted, so a click meant for an island row was taken by the page underneath before Blanc ever saw it.

Clicking a row while a page was loading could be dropped for a second, unrelated reason: a tab-state update could rebuild the panel list between mouse-down and mouse-up, destroying the row being pressed, so the click was retargeted and the row's own handler never ran. List rebuilds are now held for the duration of a click and applied as soon as it completes.
Large tab collections now scroll inside the expanded island, keeping the footer and all controls visible.

Summoning the island with ⌘L now expands it in place, on the same anchor as clicking it. It previously opened lower down with the resting island still visible above it, which read as a separate floating window rather than the same control opening.

⌘L now closes the expanded island as well as opening it, so the same shortcut puts it away. A half-typed query is never discarded — pressing it again there re-selects what you typed, as an address bar does.
Removed the overlay background-colour workaround introduced in 1.0.4. Electron parses eight-digit colours as
AARRGGBB

, so the value it set was fully transparent and never had the effect its comment described. The 1.0.5 panel-centering change is kept — it was not the fix, but it is correct and simpler than what it replaced.

Shadow-DOM drag regions remain unsupported. A page can declare a draggable region inside a shadow root, and no styling the browser applies from outside reaches into one, so a region declared there still takes clicks aimed at the island. Closing this needs a fix below the web layer and is tracked separately.

The release notes for Blanc 1.0.4 and 1.0.5 each claimed to have fixed this issue and were wrong. Neither the overlay background layer nor the panel's centering method was responsible. Both of those releases have been annotated with a correction rather than rewritten.

Blanc v0.22.0 turns the Island into a full search surface. Start typing in ⌘L and Blanc now blends your open tabs, groups, Favorites, and history with live suggestions from the search engine you chose in Settings; arrow through the six-row list or press Enter to search exactly what you typed. Suggestions can be switched off, and private tabs, pasted text, addresses, local paths, and sensitive-looking input never leave the device for autocomplete.

Tabs synced from your other Blanc devices now carry their site icons too. The source device converts each favicon into a tiny inert PNG inside a separate end-to-end-encrypted sidecar, so another device never contacts a remote tab's site just to draw its row; strict budgets, cancellation, mixed-version compatibility, and graceful fallback keep this cosmetic layer from interfering with tab sync.

Blanc v0.20.0 introduces Tab Sync: see your open tabs from your other devices. Turn on "share this device's open tabs" under Settings → Sync and each machine publishes a snapshot of its tabs — browse them from the ⌘L panel, the Quick Switcher, or the start page on any synced device, and open one locally with a click. It's a menu, not a mirror: nothing ever force-opens or closes a tab on another machine.

Sharing is off by default and per-device, private tabs never leave the machine, and like the rest of Profile Sync the snapshots are end-to-end encrypted — the sync server only ever stores ciphertext it cannot read.

Blanc v0.17.0 adds two privacy features that respect the VPN or proxy you already use: WebRTC leak protection and optional encrypted DNS (DoH).

Encrypted DNS hides your DNS lookups from the network in transit to the resolver you choose. It does not hide the sites you visit — destination IPs stay visible to your network — and choosing a provider is a trust decision. Automatic mode upgrades opportunistically and can fall back to unencrypted DNS; only the named-provider and custom positions are strict.
WebRTC leak protection keeps WebRTC from exposing addresses beyond your default connection, with an optional "disable direct UDP" mode for use behind an application proxy.
